title: Use of the HFCVD-CSVT Technique to Obtain Nanostructured Tungsten Oxide with Bundles-, Flowers-, Nanospheres- and Nanowires-Like Morphologies
content: Semiconductor nanostructured materials are widely studied due to the versatility of their physicochemical properties, which make it possible to use these properties in diverse applications such as gas sensors, photovoltaic cells, and electrochromic devices. For example, nanostructured tungsten oxide is a semiconductor material whose electrical and gas-chromic properties change when it comes into contact with contaminating gases. On the other hand, tungsten oxide can be synthesized using the Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) technique. For this, we use a reactor equipped with two modules that allow us to use the Hot Filament Chemical Vapor Deposition (HFCVD) and Close-Space Vapor Transport (CSVT) techniques, which are variants of the CVD method [1, 2].
